u0396.gist: On 14 October 2026, CCEA approved 10955230 Canada Inc. (Fairfax group) to buy 60.72% of IDBI Bank for about ₹52,878.08 crore.
facts: Buyer: 10955230 Canada Inc.; parent company Fairfax Financial Holdings Limited.
Stake sold: Government of India 30.48% + LIC 30.24% = 60.72%.
Bid ₹81 per share vs benchmark ₹75.99 (average of two independent valuations).
After the sale: Government about 15%, LIC about 19%.
Started as Industrial Development Bank of India on 1 July 1964; banking company from 1 October 2004.
RBI classed it a private sector bank from 21 January 2019, after LIC bought 51%.
u0396.hook: 60.72 = 30.48 (Govt) + 30.24 (LIC): two near-30s add up to about 61.
u0396.trap: CCEA (Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs) approved the buyer; the deal is still subject to regulatory conditions.

mcq.q: Which company was approved in October 2026 as the buyer for the strategic sale of a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank?
mcq.why: CCEA approved 10955230 Canada Inc., whose parent is Fairfax Financial Holdings Limited.

mcq.q: In the IDBI Bank strategic sale approved in October 2026, what was the approved bid per share?
mcq.why: Bid was ₹81 per share against a benchmark of ₹75.99 per share.

u0397.gist: The 57th GST Council meeting (New Delhi, 8 October 2026), chaired by Nirmala Sitharaman, recommended simpler registration, faster refunds and easier compliance.
facts: 57th GST Council meeting: New Delhi, October 8, 2026; chair Nirmala Sitharaman.
Simpler registration form FORM GST REG-01; auto-approval of amendments except Principal Place of Business (PPoB).
Rule 14B: simple registration route for small e-commerce sellers.
Refund acknowledgement/deficiency memo time cut from 15 days to 10 days.
Minimum tax amount for issuing a show-cause notice: ₹10,000.
ITC on input services received on or after 1 November 2026 to count for inverted duty refunds.

mcq.q: At the 57th GST Council meeting in October 2026, what minimum tax amount was recommended for issuing a show-cause notice?
mcq.why: The Council recommended a minimum tax amount of ₹10,000 for a show-cause notice.

u0398.gist: At its 63rd meeting (5-7 October 2026), RBI's MPC under Governor Sanjay Malhotra raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%.
facts: Repo rate up 25 basis points: 5.25% to 5.50%; decision unanimous.
From 7 October 2026: SDF 5.25%; MSF and Bank Rate 5.75%.
RBI forecast for FY 2026–27: real GDP growth 7.1%, CPI inflation 5.2%, core inflation 4.4%.
Actual Q1 FY 2026–27 (April–June 2026) real GDP growth: 7.8% (MoSPI).
Inflation target 4% (band 2% to 6%) for 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031.
September CPI (released 12 October 2026, provisional): headline 5.54%, food 7.74%; base 2024=100.
u0398.trap: 7.1% is RBI's full-year FY 2026–27 forecast; 7.8% is the actual Q1 growth. 5.2% is projected CPI; 5.54% is September's actual.

mcq.q: At the 63rd MPC meeting in October 2026, the RBI's policy repo rate was changed to:
mcq.why: The MPC raised the repo rate by 25 basis points, from 5.25% to 5.50%.

mcq.q: For the period 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031, India's notified CPI inflation target is:
mcq.why: Target is 4%, with a lower tolerance limit of 2% and upper limit of 6%.

u0399.gist: The Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026, in force from 1 October 2026, names different authorities for late registration by length of delay.
facts: Amends Section 13 of the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969.
Presidential assent: August 6, 2026; in force: October 1, 2026.
Delay over one year but within two years: order of DM, SDM or authorised Executive Magistrate (Section 13(3)).
Delay over two years: order of a Judicial Magistrate of the First Class (Section 13(3A)).
Normal reporting time: 21 days; registration within 30 days needs a late fee.
Start date notified by Registrar General, India (MHA) through S.O. 5081(E), 16 September 2026.
u0399.trap: Under the 2023 amendment every delay over one year needed a DM/SDM order; the 2026 Act shifts over-two-year cases to a Judicial Magistrate.

mcq.q: Under the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026, a birth reported more than two years late can be registered only on the order of:
o: Judicial Magistrate of the First Class
mcq.why: New Section 13(3A): delays over two years need a Judicial Magistrate of the First Class.

u0400.gist: PMJDY, India's National Mission for Financial Inclusion launched on 28 August 2014, completed 12 years on 28 August 2026 with 59.09 crore accounts.
facts: Launched by PM Narendra Modi on 28 August 2014.
Accounts: 14.72 crore (2015) to 59.09 crore (19 August 2026), about fourfold.
Women hold 32.92 crore accounts (about 55.7%); rural and semi-urban 45.95 crore (77.8%).
Deposits: ₹15,670 crore (March 2015) to ₹3,16,514 crore (August 2026); average ₹5,356 per account.
Accident cover ₹2 lakh for accounts opened after August 28, 2018; overdraft up to ₹10,000.
Guinness record (January 2015): 18,096,130 accounts opened in one week, August 23-29, 2014.
u0400.hook: Same birthday: launched 28 August 2014, 12 years on 28 August 2026.

mcq.q: As of 19 August 2026, how many bank accounts had been opened under PMJDY?
mcq.why: Accounts rose from 14.72 crore in 2015 to 59.09 crore by 19 August 2026.

u0401.gist: Under PMGKAY, eligible beneficiaries now get food subsidy as programmable Digital Rupee (e₹) tokens in CBDC wallets instead of bank transfers.
facts: CBDC-based DBT for PMGKAY launched in Chandigarh and Dadra & Nagar Haveli on August 14, 2026.
Launched by Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan.
Pilots: Gujarat by Amit Shah (February 15, 2026); Puducherry by Prahlad Joshi (February 26, 2026).
Digital Rupee (e₹) is a tokenised digital rupee issued by RBI as a CBDC.
Chandigarh was an early adopter of food-subsidy DBT in September 2015.
u0401.trap: Pilot began in Gujarat (February 2026); the PMGKAY launch was in Chandigarh and Dadra & Nagar Haveli (14 August 2026).

mcq.q: Where was CBDC-based DBT for PMGKAY beneficiaries launched on August 14, 2026?
mcq.why: The Government launched it in Chandigarh and Dadra & Nagar Haveli on August 14, 2026.

u0402.gist: The Government approved RBI's proposal for field trials of ₹10 and ₹20 polymer banknotes; existing paper notes stay legal tender.
facts: RBI proposed one billion notes of each: 200 crore notes, face value about ₹3,000 crore.
Proposal under Sections 24 (denominations) and 25 (design, form, materials) of the RBI Act, 1934.
BRBNMPL, an RBI subsidiary, started procuring polymer substrate.
Australia first issued a polymer banknote in 1988; more than 60 countries use them.
Currency in circulation up 12% to ₹41.23 lakh crore (end-March 2026); ₹500 notes about 86% of value.
Printing cost fell nearly 24% to ₹4,875 crore in 2025–26.
u0402.trap: Section 24 = denominations; Section 25 = design, form and materials.
u0402.check: Coins in circulation printed as '₹40,814' with no unit (crore?).

mcq.q: India plans field trials of ₹10 and ₹20 polymer banknotes. Which country first issued a polymer banknote, in 1988?
mcq.why: Australia first issued a polymer banknote in 1988.

u0403.gist: The Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 2026 (in force 1 October 2026) replaces the 1891 Act and accepts physical, electronic and digital bank records as evidence.
facts: Replaces the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891 with a technology-neutral framework.
Lok Sabha passed it 5 August 2026, Rajya Sabha 10 August; assent 13 August 2026.
Bankers' books include records at off-site, virtual, cloud, backup and disaster recovery locations.
'Banks' include post office savings bank and money order offices.
Certified copies are prima facie (first-look), not conclusive, evidence.
NBFCs, payment aggregators and fintechs covered only if notified or under another law.

mcq.q: The Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 2026, which came into force on October 1, 2026, replaced the Bankers' Books Evidence Act of which year?
mcq.why: The 2026 Act replaces the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891.

u0404.gist: The Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026 (Lok Sabha, 3 August 2026) would replace the 1959 Act and make ISI a statutory body corporate.
facts: Introduced in Lok Sabha on 3 August 2026; replaces the 1959 Act (in force April 1, 1960).
ISI stays an institution of national importance under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
President of India would be the Visitor; can order reviews and nominate the Board Chairperson.
An 11-member Board would replace the 33-member Council.
Board: Chairperson, government representatives, four external experts and four ISI representatives.
The Director would be the Chief Executive Officer.
u0404.hook: 11 replaces 33: the new Board is one-third the size of the old Council.
hindi: Institution of national importance (राष्ट्रीय महत्व का संस्थान)

mcq.q: Under the Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026, the 33-member Council would be replaced by a Board of how many members?
mcq.why: An 11-member Board would replace the 33-member Council.

u0405.gist: The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 replaced MGNREGA from July 1, 2026 and raised the rural job guarantee from 100 to 125 days a year.
facts: Full name: Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025.
In force across rural India from July 1, 2026; repealed MGNREGA, 2005.
Guarantee raised from 100 to 125 days per year; wage floor ₹300/day for 2026–27.
Funding: 90:10 for Northeastern and Himalayan States; 60:40 for other States/UTs with legislatures.
Shivraj Singh Chouhan released over ₹25,000 crore as first instalment, the 'Mother Sanction'.
FY 2026–27 Central share ₹95,692.31 crore (Budget Estimate); total outlay over ₹1.51 lakh crore.
u0405.hook: VB-G RAM G = Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar And Ajeevika Mission (Gramin). Motto: 'Rozgar Bhi, Samman Bhi'.
u0405.trap: Old MGNREGA guarantee = 100 days; new Act = 125 days. UTs without legislatures get full Central funding.

mcq.q: Under the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, in force from July 1, 2026, how many days of wage employment are guaranteed per rural household per financial year?
mcq.why: The Act raises the guarantee from 100 to 125 days per financial year.

mcq.q: Under the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, what is the Centre–State funding ratio for States other than Northeastern and Himalayan States?
mcq.why: 90:10 for Northeastern/Himalayan States; 60:40 for other States and UTs with legislatures.

u0406.gist: MoSPI's Provisional Estimates (5 June 2026) put India's real GDP growth for 2025–26 at 7.7%, with fourth-quarter growth at 7.8%.
facts: Released by MoSPI on June 5, 2026, with fourth-quarter (January–March) estimates.
Real GDP 2025–26: ₹323.12 lakh crore vs ₹299.89 lakh crore in 2024–25 (growth 7.7%).
Nominal GDP 2025–26: ₹346.36 lakh crore, growth 8.9%.
Real GVA growth 7.9%; nominal GVA growth 9.1% (2025–26).
Fourth-quarter 2025–26 real GDP growth estimated at 7.8%.
u0406.trap: Full-year 2025–26 real growth 7.7% vs Q4 growth 7.8%; real GDP 7.7% vs nominal GDP 8.9%.

mcq.q: According to MoSPI's Provisional Estimates released on June 5, 2026, India's real GDP growth for 2025–26 is estimated at:
mcq.why: Real GDP rose from ₹299.89 lakh crore to ₹323.12 lakh crore: growth 7.7%.

u0407.gist: On 27 February 2026, MoSPI released a new GDP series with base year 2022–23, replacing 2011–12, as a recent normal post-COVID year.
facts: New base year 2022–23 replaced 2011–12; released by MoSPI on 27 February 2026.
Q1 FY 2026-27 real GDP: ₹81.36 lakh crore, growth 7.8% (vs 6.9% a year earlier).
Q1 FY 2026-27 nominal GDP: ₹88.27 lakh crore, growth 10.3%.
Q1 2026-27 growth: GFCF 11.9%, exports 12.0%, PFCE 7.1%.
u0407.trap: New base year 2022–23; old base year 2011–12.
u0407.check: Release dated 27 February 2026, yet the text quotes Q1 FY 2026-27 (April–June 2026) figures; these must come from a later release.

mcq.q: In February 2026, MoSPI released India's new GDP series with which base year?
mcq.why: The new series has base year 2022–23, replacing the 2011–12 series.

u0408.gist: National Health Accounts 2022–23: India's total health spending was ₹8,81,359 crore (3.37% of GDP); households paid 43.41% out of pocket.
facts: Total Health Expenditure (THE) 2022–23: ₹8,81,359 crore = 3.37% of GDP; ₹6,373 per person.
Government Health Expenditure: ₹3,85,332 crore = 43.72% of THE, 1.48% of GDP.
Out-of-Pocket Expenditure: ₹3,82,629 crore = 43.41% of THE; ₹2,767 per person.
Current Health Expenditure 87.00% and capital 13.00% of THE; uses System of Health Accounts 2011.
By level of care (share of Current Health Expenditure): primary ~46%, secondary ~34%, tertiary ~15%.
In government current health spending, primary care took 51%.
u0408.trap: Government share (43.72%) and out-of-pocket share (43.41%) are very close; government is slightly higher.
hindi: Out-of-pocket expenditure (जेब से होने वाला खर्च)

mcq.q: According to the National Health Accounts Estimates 2022–23, India's Total Health Expenditure as a share of GDP was:
mcq.why: THE was ₹8,81,359 crore, equal to 3.37% of GDP.

u0409.gist: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 completed ten years in 2026, moving India from delay-based liquidation towards reviving companies.
facts: IBC enacted May 28, 2016; IBBI set up October 1, 2016.
Till March 31, 2026: 8,987 cases admitted, 7,102 closed, 1,419 resolution plans approved.
4,099 companies rescued; creditors realised more than ₹4 lakh crore.
Realisation about 95% of fair value and about 167% of liquidation value.
FY 2024-25: banks recovered ₹1.04 lakh crore; ₹0.54 lakh crore (52.4%) via IBC.
Banks' gross NPA ratio (domestic): 2.15% on September 30, 2025.
hindi: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (दिवाला और शोधन अक्षमता संहिता)

mcq.q: The IBC completed ten years in 2026. When was the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India established?
mcq.why: IBC was enacted on May 28, 2016; IBBI was established on October 1, 2016.

u0410.gist: UPI completed 10 years on April 11, 2026 since its 2016 pilot launch, growing from an experiment into the backbone of India's digital economy.
facts: Pilot launch: 11 April 2016; 10 years completed April 11, 2026.
Record 22.64 billion transactions in March 2026; 24.51 billion in August 2026.
Over 81% of India's retail payment volume in FY 2024-25.
FY 2025–26: 24,161.69 crore transactions worth about ₹314 lakh crore.
Around 85% of India's digital payments (FY 2025–26); about 49% of global real-time payments (2025).
u0410.check: March 2026 (22.64 billion) is called the all-time high, but August 2026 shows 24.51 billion.

mcq.q: UPI completed 10 years in April 2026. In which year was its pilot launched?
mcq.why: UPI's pilot launch was on 11 April 2016.

u0411.gist: The Income-tax Act, 2025 came into force on 1 April 2026, replacing the Income-tax Act, 1961 with simpler language and a single 'Tax Year'.
facts: In force from 1 April 2026; replaces the six-decade-old Income-tax Act, 1961.
'Tax Year' replaces 'Assessment Year' and 'Previous Year'.
CBDT notified the Income-tax Rules, 2026 to implement the Act.
Form 130 replaces Form 16 (TDS certificate issued by employers).
New Act: 536 Sections, 23 Chapters, 16 Schedules; TDS/TCS in sections 392,393 and 394.
New regime (AY 2026-27): zero tax up to ₹12 lakh; standard deduction ₹75,000 (was ₹50,000).
u0411.trap: Form 130 is new; Form 16 is the old TDS certificate. Zero-tax limit ₹12 lakh (new) vs ₹7 lakh (old).
u0411.check: 1961 Act shown as '819+ sections and 298 Chapters' and gross direct tax 2025–26 as ₹7.99 lakh crore; both look doubtful.

mcq.q: Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, in force from 1 April 2026, which form replaces Form 16 (the TDS certificate issued by employers)?
mcq.why: Form 130 replaces the traditional Form 16.

u0412.gist: The 16th Finance Commission (chair Arvind Panagariya), covering 2026–27 to 2030–31, kept States' share of the divisible pool at 41%; UP's share is 17.62%.
facts: Constitutional body under Article 280; 16th FC set up December 31, 2023 under Dr. Arvind Panagariya.
Report submitted 17 November 2025; tabled in Parliament 1 February 2026.
States' vertical share stays 41%; weights: income distance 42.5%, population (2011) 17.5%.
Total grants about ₹9.47 lakh crore for 2026–31; ₹7.91 lakh crore for local bodies.
Fiscal deficit: Centre to 3.5% of GDP by 2030–31; States' ceiling stays 3% of GSDP.
UP's share: 17.94% (15th FC) to 17.62% (16th FC), highest among States listed.
u0412.trap: 41% = States' vertical share (unchanged); 42.5% = weight for income distance. The 16th FC dropped revenue deficit, sector-specific and state-specific grants.

mcq.q: Who chaired the 16th Finance Commission, constituted on December 31, 2023?
mcq.why: The 16th FC was constituted under the chairmanship of Dr. Arvind Panagariya.

mcq.q: As recommended by the 16th Finance Commission (2026–31), the States' vertical share in the divisible pool of Union taxes is:
mcq.why: The Commission recommended the States' vertical share remain 41% of the divisible pool.

u0413.gist: On 14 October 2026, Cabinet approved NSAP for FY 2026–27 to 2030–31 (₹53,428 crore) and renamed it Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana.
facts: NSAP launched 15 August 1995; helps poor elderly, widows, disabled and families losing a breadwinner.
Outlay ₹53,428 crore over five years (FY 2026–27 to FY 2030–31).
Renamed: NSAP to Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana; IGNOAPS to PM Vriddhavastha Pension Yojana.
Disability pension: ₹375/month (age 0–79), ₹625/month (80 and above).
Disability threshold cut from 80% to benchmark disability of at least 40%; eligible from birth.
3.20 crore beneficiaries across 36 States and UTs.
u0413.trap: 80 appears twice: age 80+ gets ₹625; 80% was the old disability threshold (now 40%).

mcq.q: In October 2026, the Union Cabinet approved renaming the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) as:
mcq.why: NSAP becomes Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana; the others are renamed sub-schemes.

mcq.q: Under the NSAP changes approved in October 2026, the disability pension eligibility threshold was reduced from 80% to:
mcq.why: Threshold reduced from 80% to benchmark disability of at least 40%, from birth.

u0414.gist: The CRS 2024 report (released 1 July 2026) shows India registered an estimated 99.1% of births and 99.4% of deaths in 2024.
facts: Released by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India on July 1, 2026.
Registration level 2024: births 99.1%, deaths 99.4% (2000: 56.2% and 48.7%).
Sex Ratio at Birth: 933 females per 1,000 males (excluding Sikkim).
Highest SRB: Arunachal Pradesh (1,050); lowest: Nagaland (806).
Registered births rose by 2,66,319 (about 1.1%) from 2023 to 2024.
Stillbirths fell 19.3% to 81,117; infant deaths fell from 1,45,992 to 1,20,992.
u0414.trap: SRB 933 comes from registered events; do not work it out from the 52.5% male / 47.5% female split.
hindi: Sex ratio at birth (जन्म के समय लिंगानुपात)

mcq.q: According to the CRS 2024 report, which State/UT recorded the highest registered Sex Ratio at Birth?
mcq.why: Arunachal Pradesh topped with 1,050; Kerala was fifth with 970.

mcq.q: As per the CRS 2024 report, India's Sex Ratio at Birth (females per 1,000 males) based on registered events was:
mcq.why: SRB stood at 933 females per 1,000 males, excluding Sikkim.

u0415.gist: NFHS-6 (2023–24) fact sheets, released 29 May 2026, show more institutional births, better vaccination and women's empowerment; TFR stays 2.0.
facts: Released May 29, 2026 by the Health Ministry; IIPS, Mumbai surveyed 6.79 lakh households in 715 districts.
95.9% of pregnant women got antenatal care; first-trimester care 70.0% to 76.2%; at least four visits 58.5% to 65.2%.
TFR stayed 2.0 (urban 1.6, rural 2.1); institutional deliveries 88.6% to 90.6%.
Full vaccination (12–23 months) 83.8% to 87.1%; rotavirus 36.4% to 85.4%.
Stunting fell 35.5% to 29.3%; overweight/obese women rose 24.0% to 30.7%.
Women using internet 33.3% to 64.3%; spousal violence 29.2% to 22.3%.
u0415.hook: Women's internet use nearly doubled: 33.3 to 64.3.
u0415.trap: NFHS-6 survey was done in 2023–24 but released in 2026; it is compared with NFHS-5 (2019–21).

mcq.q: Which institute conducted the sixth National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6), whose fact sheets were released in May 2026?
o: Office of the Registrar General of India
International Institute for Population Sciences, Mumbai
mcq.why: NFHS-6 was conducted during 2023–24 by IIPS, Mumbai.

mcq.q: According to NFHS-6 (released May 2026), India's Total Fertility Rate is:
mcq.why: India's TFR remained at 2.0 (urban 1.6, rural 2.1).

u0416.gist: The SRS Bulletin 2024, released by the Registrar General of India on 20 May 2026, shows birth rate 18.3, death rate 6.4 and IMR 24.
facts: Released May 20, 2026 with the Special Bulletin on Maternal Mortality (2022-24).
Birth rate 18.3 (2014: 21.0); highest Bihar 26.8, lowest Andaman and Nicobar 9.9.
Death rate 6.4; highest Chhattisgarh 8.4, lowest Chandigarh 3.9.
IMR 24 (2014: 39); highest Chhattisgarh 36, lowest Manipur 2.
MMR 87 per 100,000 live births (2022-24) vs 130 in 2014-16.
Natural growth rate 11.9; Bihar 20.8 (high), Kerala 3.9 (low).
u0416.trap: Chhattisgarh tops both death rate (8.4) and IMR (36). 3.9 is twice: Chandigarh's death rate and Kerala's natural growth rate.

mcq.q: According to the SRS Bulletin 2024, which State recorded the highest Infant Mortality Rate?
mcq.why: Chhattisgarh recorded the highest IMR at 36.

mcq.q: As per the SRS Special Bulletin (2022-24), India's maternal mortality ratio per 100,000 live births was:
mcq.why: MMR was 87 in SRS 2022-24, compared with 130 in 2014-16.

u0417.gist: MoSPI unveiled a new logo and a citizen-friendly mascot on 1 January 2026 to modernise its identity and build trust in official statistics.
facts: New logo and mascot unveiled by MoSPI on 1 January 2026.
Ashoka Chakra = truth, transparency, good governance; ₹ symbol at the centre.
Logo message: 'Data for Development'; colours saffron, white, green and deep blue.
Mascot 'सांख्यिकी' to be used in National Sample Surveys by the NSS wing of NSO.
Finance Ministry unveiled a common logo for Regional Rural Banks on 18 December 2025.
u0417.check: Mascot name is printed with a broken character ('सांख्य⼿की'); likely सांख्यिकी.

mcq.q: What message does the new MoSPI logo, unveiled on 1 January 2026, carry?
mcq.why: The logo carries the message 'Data for Development'.

u0418.gist: The Agriculture Ministry held the National Conference on Agriculture for Kharif Campaign 2026 on 28-29 May 2026 at NASC Complex, Pusa, New Delhi.
facts: Held May 28-29, 2026 at NASC Complex, Pusa, New Delhi.
Chaired by Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan.
Agriculture Ministers from 22 States took part, called a historic first.
Khet Bachao Abhiyan ran from 1 June to 30 June 2026.
Another nationwide campaign announced for October 22 – November 30, 2026.

mcq.q: Following the Kharif Campaign 2026 conference, which campaign ran from 1 June to 30 June 2026?
mcq.why: Khet Bachao Abhiyan was launched on 1 June 2026 and ran till 30 June 2026.

u0419.gist: On 13 May 2026, CCEA raised MSP for all 14 Kharif crops for 2026–27; sunflower seed got the biggest rise (₹622 per quintal).
facts: CCEA chaired by PM Narendra Modi; Marketing Season 2026–27.
Biggest MSP rises: sunflower seed ₹622, cotton ₹557, nigerseed ₹515, sesamum ₹500 per quintal.
Paddy (common) MSP ₹2,441 and Grade A ₹2,461 per quintal.
Highest MSP: sesamum ₹10,346, then nigerseed ₹10,052 per quintal.
Union Budget 2018–19 rule: MSP at least 1.5 times the all-India weighted average (A2+FL) cost.
Highest margin over cost: moong (61%), then bajra and maize (56% each).
u0419.trap: Biggest increase = sunflower seed (₹622); highest MSP = sesamum (₹10,346).

mcq.q: For the Kharif Marketing Season 2026–27, which crop received the highest increase in MSP?
mcq.why: Sunflower seed got the biggest rise, ₹622 per quintal.

mcq.q: Which Kharif crop has the highest MSP for Marketing Season 2026–27?
mcq.why: Sesamum has the highest MSP at ₹10,346 per quintal.

u0420.gist: Third Advance Estimates (27 May 2026) put India's 2025–26 foodgrain output at a record 376.563 million tonnes, up 5.3% on last year.
facts: Released May 27, 2026 by Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan.
Foodgrains 376.563 million tonnes vs 357.732 million tonnes in 2024–25 (about 18.8 million tonnes more).
Rice record 154.024 million tonnes; wheat 120.657 million tonnes.
Sugarcane record 500.063 million tonnes; groundnut record 13.074 million tonnes; oilseeds 43.059 million tonnes.
UP first in rice (198.05), wheat (358.77) and sugarcane (2,296.99) lakh tonnes.
Other leaders: maize and pulses Madhya Pradesh; oilseeds Rajasthan; cotton Maharashtra; jute West Bengal.
u0420.hook: UP's triple crown: No. 1 in rice, wheat and sugarcane.
u0420.trap: Cotton bale = 170 kg; jute bale = 180 kg.

mcq.q: As per the Third Advance Estimates for 2025–26, India's total foodgrain production is estimated at:
mcq.why: Foodgrains at a record 376.563 million tonnes, up 5.3% from 357.732 million tonnes.

mcq.q: According to the 2025–26 Third Advance Estimates, which State ranks first in rice production?
mcq.why: UP leads with 198.05 lakh tonnes, ahead of Telangana and West Bengal.

u0421.gist: Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics 2025, released on National Milk Day (26 November 2025), shows India 1st in milk with 247.87 million tonnes.
facts: Released November 26, 2025 (National Milk Day) by MoS Prof. S.P. Singh Baghel.
Based on the Integrated Sample Survey, March 1, 2024 to February 28, 2025.
Milk 2024-25: 247.87 million tonnes (+3.58%), India 1st; 485 g/day per person.
Eggs: 149.11 billion, India 2nd; meat: 10.50 million tonnes, India 4th.
Top States: milk – Uttar Pradesh (15.66%); eggs – Andhra Pradesh; wool – Rajasthan (47.85%).
Livestock GVA up about 195% (2014–15 to 2023–24); 31% of agricultural GVA.

mcq.q: According to Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics 2025, India's estimated milk production in 2024-25 was:
mcq.why: Milk was 247.87 million tonnes, up 3.58% from 239.30 million tonnes in 2023-24.

mcq.q: According to Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics 2025, which State is the top milk producer?
mcq.why: Uttar Pradesh leads with 15.66%, ahead of Rajasthan (14.82%).

u0421.trap: UP is first in milk (15.66%) but second in meat (12.20%), behind West Bengal (12.46%).

u0422.gist: The MSMED (Amendment) Act, 2026 amends the 2006 Act to fight delayed payments, ease registration and speed up MSME dispute resolution.
facts: Introduced in Rajya Sabha on 28 July 2026 by MSME Minister Jitan Ram Manjhi.
Rajya Sabha passed 3 August, Lok Sabha 7 August, assent 13 August 2026; Act No. 16 of 2026.
CPSEs must settle MSME invoices through TReDS (RBI-regulated invoice platform).
Mediation within 90 days; failed mediation goes to arbitration within 30 days.
Buyer challenging an award deposits 75%; court releases at least 50% after six months.
Memorandum filing free and voluntary; TReDS discounted invoices ₹40,000 crore (2021–22) to ₹3.47 lakh crore (2025–26).
u0422.trap: Bill was introduced first in the Rajya Sabha (28 July), not the Lok Sabha.
hindi: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (सूक्ष्म, लघु एवं मध्यम उद्यम)

mcq.q: Under the MSMED (Amendment) Act, 2026, Central Public Sector Enterprises must settle MSME invoices through which platform?
mcq.why: CPSEs must settle MSME invoices through TReDS, regulated by the RBI.

u0423.gist: Cabinet approved the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (₹62,500 crore, FY 2026–27 to 2030–31) on 15 July 2026, succeeding PLI-LSEM.
facts: Cabinet approval July 15, 2026; MeitY notified it on August 21, 2026.
Outlay ₹62,500 crore; runs five years, FY 2026–27 to FY 2030–31.
Succeeds PLI-LSEM, which ended 31 March 2026.
Incentive 2.25% to 5% on sales; up to 1.5% extra for local sourcing; Indian brands 3% extra.
Electronics production: ₹1.90 lakh crore (2014–15) to ₹13.11 lakh crore (2025–26, estimate).
Electronic goods: India's third-largest export category, USD 47.96 billion in FY 2025–26.
hindi: Production Linked Incentive (उत्पादन से जुड़ा प्रोत्साहन)

mcq.q: The Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (MPMS), approved by the Union Cabinet in July 2026, has a budgetary outlay of:
mcq.why: MPMS has a budgetary outlay of ₹62,500 crore for five years.
